proposal.hypothesis: Replace allocation-heavy per-record aggregation with borrowed-key hash aggregation: split the three fields without collecting a Vec, keep endpoint slices in the standard randomized HashMap, allocate each endpoint once when producing the result, and sort only the unique output rows. Development evidence spans 512 and 8192 records with roughly 8 to 3554 distinct endpoints; removing allocations on repeated records should improve both sizes, while expected constant-time lookup should reduce the high-cardinality tree-comparison cost. Exact numeric, Unicode-control, line-ending and invalid-row validation is unchanged.
proposal.notes: Fresh model-authored proposal from the exported baseline development evidence. Static source inspection only; no compilation, correctness execution or benchmarks were run by this proposal author. The standard library randomized hasher is retained, so measurements include its normal seed variation and maintain its untrusted-input defenses. Risks: hash initialization and the final sort may cost more on tiny or mostly-unique inputs; the HashMap can use more peak memory than a BTreeMap. Borrowed keys do not escape this call, and output ordering remains lexicographic. No unsafe code, global state, persistent caching, input-specific answers, driver changes or dependency additions.

proposal.hypothesis: Fuse delimiter discovery, field validation, and numeric conversion into one allocation-free byte parser while retaining the incumbent borrowed-key standard HashMap and final ordering. Round-1 development measurements improve all 8192-record cases (mean case log ratios about -0.10 to -0.54), but the 512-record high-cardinality cases still regress (+0.08 to +0.17); removing repeated parser scans should lower per-record work without adding another cardinality heuristic. ASCII endpoint control checks are fused with the first-TAB scan, and non-ASCII endpoints still use char::is_control. Numeric grammar and conversion share a scan. Status values reject monotonically above 599; byte fields of at most 19 digits cannot overflow u64, and longer fields use checked arithmetic to preserve both u64::MAX and arbitrarily many leading zeroes.
proposal.notes: Fresh model-authored revision based only on the exported round-1-clean application and development evidence. No compile, correctness execution, profiling or benchmark was run by the proposal author. The timing pattern suggests remaining parsing and fixed map/sort overhead but does not establish a profile. This change deliberately targets parsing only; hash/sort setup cost on small inputs may remain. Risks: a scalar endpoint scan may be slower than the standard delimiter implementation on very long endpoints, non-ASCII endpoints need a second control scan, and unusual long numeric fields pay checked-arithmetic overhead. Exact LF/final-LF and single terminal-CR handling remain unchanged; signs, whitespace, Unicode digits, extra TABs and overflow remain invalid. Only ASCII TAB boundaries slice str. No unsafe code, custom hasher, global state, caching, dependency or driver changes.

proposal.hypothesis: Validate endpoint control characters only on first insertion into the per-call aggregation map. Existing keys necessarily passed the same char::is_control predicate, and exact str equality certifies subsequent occurrences without rescanning their characters. This enables the standard split_once TAB search instead of a scalar endpoint scan on every record. Round-2 development evidence leaves Unicode-endpoint cases at roughly 92-105 ns per record versus about 60-76 ns for low-cardinality ASCII cases; repeated Unicode decoding and per-record endpoint scanning are a concrete remaining cost, although this is not profiling evidence. The change can also benefit repeated ASCII endpoints while leaving numeric parsing, randomized hashing and final sorting unchanged.
proposal.notes: Fresh model-authored proposal based on round-2-preselection exported development evidence. No local compile, test or benchmark was run. This is a single endpoint-validation-hoisting change, not a workload-size heuristic: the existing HashMap itself proves which exact endpoints are valid. Invalid endpoints are never inserted, and invalid row counts remain per occurrence. There is no global or cross-call cache or extra validation cache. Full char::is_control semantics remain authoritative for both ASCII and Unicode on first insertion; starts_with slash is checked on every row. Numeric overflow, signs, leading zeroes, field count and line-ending behavior remain unchanged. Risks: mostly-unique endpoints reduce validation reuse, and rows with valid numbers but invalid endpoint controls now perform a hash lookup before rejection, which may regress heavily malformed input. Standard hasher seed variability remains. The anticipated incremental gain is credible but unmeasured and must exceed the controller threshold.

proposal.hypothesis: Refine the endpoint-validation-hoisting proposal with direct recognition of the status field grammar. A valid status is exactly zero or more leading ASCII zeroes followed by [1-5][0-9][0-9] and TAB, so status arithmetic and the per-digit upper-bound loop can be replaced by direct byte checks while preserving every accepted spelling. Combined with validating each new endpoint once using char::is_control, this removes redundant parsing work on repeated and distinct endpoints. Round-3 development data reduced the Unicode-endpoint cost from round-2 roughly 92-105 ns/record to roughly 64-76, but remaining ASCII repeated-key costs around 55-65 ns/record and essentially unchanged high-cardinality costs leave plausible common-path headroom. Direct status recognition applies to all records rather than a workload-size threshold.
proposal.notes: Fresh model-authored final proposal; static inspection only, no compile/test/benchmark by the proposal author. The actual accepted base is round 2. Round 3 passed correctness and had favorable development timing, but was not promoted because its uncertainty lower bound narrowly missed the prespecified 1.05x gate. This full-file proposal retains that unaccepted endpoint mechanism and adds exact status-grammar recognition; the combined improvement is unmeasured and is not claimed to clear the gate. No thresholds or repetitions are being changed to reverse the prior decision. Status 000100..000599 remains accepted, including arbitrarily many leading zeroes; statuses below 100, above 599, signs, overflow-sized nonzero values, extra digits and non-ASCII spellings remain rejected. Byte-count arithmetic, line endings, field count and output sorting remain unchanged. Standard randomized hashing and its seed variability remain. Risks inherited from endpoint validation hoisting include less reuse for unique keys and hashing numerically valid rows with invalid endpoint controls before rejection. Leading-zero-heavy status strings still require a linear scan; performance gains may be smaller than expected without profiling. No unsafe code, global caching, extra dependencies or case-specific paths.
